narrative:
The model determined that you have an 81% probability of representing a bad credit risk. This high likelihood led directly to the denial of your loan application.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, your credit history, and the purpose of the loan. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the single biggest reason for the rejection. While only 12.6% of approved applicants have accounts in the red, this situation strongly pushed the model toward viewing you as high risk. Your credit history of having no credits or all paid was the second most important factor. This is quite rare—only 1% of approved applicants share this profile—and it also increased the predicted risk. Finally, requesting the loan for a new car contributed to the negative decision, though less strongly than the first two factors. Most approved applicants (35%) seek loans for radio or TV, while only 16.5% request financing for a new car.

Taken together, these elements created a clear picture of elevated risk in the model's assessment. 

To improve your chances next time, focus on maintaining a positive checking account balance for several months and building a track record of timely payments on any existing obligations. Consider applying for a smaller amount or a different purpose that aligns more closely with what successful applicants typically request.
